title: AI surfaced an audience angle we had missed
whatTried: Used Gemini to turn a rough story idea into a structured content brief for a Chatelaine feature.
whatSurprisedMe: The first draft surfaced a reader question — 'what does this mean for someone already doing this?' — that our team had not explicitly considered. It reframed the angle entirely.
whatWorked: Asking the AI to critique the brief from an audience perspective was more useful than asking for a polished first draft. The critique found gaps faster than a team review would have.
whatFailed: The first version made unsupported assumptions about search volume and audience intent. It cited a trend as 'growing' without any data.
nextTime: Provide existing coverage links, audience data, and search terms before asking for recommendations. The brief gets sharper when the AI has real signal to work from.

title: RFP draft cut our turnaround from 3 days to same day
whatTried: Used Claude to draft an RFP response for a national advertiser. Pasted the RFP document, our rate card summary, and three past campaign results as context.
whatSurprisedMe: The draft was structured, on-brand, and required fewer edits than a first draft from a junior team member. The section on audience reach was nearly publishable.
whatWorked: Giving Claude the existing proposal structure as a template before asking it to fill in made the output usable immediately. It matched the advertiser's framing and language.
whatFailed: The pricing section invented numbers. It had to be deleted entirely and rebuilt manually.
nextTime: Always exclude pricing generation from the AI task. Keep the financial model as a manual step and use AI only for narrative, positioning, and packaging language.

title: Submagic captions saved two hours per episode
whatTried: Used Submagic to auto-caption a new video series for Instagram Reels instead of manually timing captions in Premiere.
whatSurprisedMe: The accuracy was high enough on the first pass that cleanup took under 10 minutes. The word-by-word highlight style performed better than our static-caption control.
whatWorked: Exporting the SRT file from Submagic and bringing it into CapCut for final branding kept the workflow flexible. We did not have to stay inside one tool.
whatFailed: The first version missed proper nouns and brand names consistently. Product names were mangled.
nextTime: Build a custom dictionary in Submagic with brand and product names before the first run. Saves three rounds of correction.

title: Subject line variants outperformed our control by 18%
whatTried: Used ChatGPT to generate 10 newsletter subject line variants for a Today's Parent issue. Ran an A/B test through Sailthru with the two strongest candidates against our usual process.
whatSurprisedMe: The winning variant used a specific number we had included in the article body but had not thought to surface in the subject line. Open rate lift was 18% above the control.
whatWorked: Asking for 10 variants and then rating them as a team before testing gave us better coverage of angles than generating one or two manually. The volume made the good ideas visible.
whatFailed: Two of the ten variants were off-brand — they were too informal for Today's Parent's voice. We would not have caught that without a team review step.
nextTime: Include voice and tone examples from recent high-performing sends before asking for variants. Cuts the editing round significantly.

title: Meeting notes agent cleared our action item backlog
whatTried: Ran Supernormal on three consecutive weekly editorial planning meetings. Used the auto-generated action items and pushed them directly into ClickUp tasks.
whatSurprisedMe: The backlog of unresolved action items became visible immediately. Supernormal surfaced three items from prior meetings that had been dropped entirely.
whatWorked: The combination of Supernormal for capture and Gemini for summarizing the pattern across all three meetings gave us a useful view of what kept recurring. We used that to fix a planning process gap.
whatFailed: Some action items were assigned to the wrong person when two people had overlapping roles in the discussion. Required manual correction.
nextTime: Introduce yourself with your name and role at the start of each meeting. Supernormal uses voice to attribute actions, and it performs better when speaker names are clear.
